cost: Sum only costs of reached route/helpers, preserving shared cached pages/host rules. Parsing linear in bytes plus id/page sorts; archive work follows decompressed size, not compressed bound. Network/process/disk/sleep costs remain unmeasured. No speedup or approximate percentage accuracy claim.

Real joins: raw::License::code and books::BookLicense::code match fetch's finite allowed strings; raw inputs match OAI gzip page naming; HTTP encode transports literal token bytes; robots uses Polite and fetch invokes Gate before downloading. Counterexample: GCS JSON numeric size becomes zero; it is not raw KB format. Book build's DNS means offline TSV construction is not a pure parser. SQL filling is sequential substitution, not DB semantics.
inverse: Inner exclusions: invalid fetch list/license prevents download setup; terminal OAI token prevents request; unknown raw license host cannot map Open. Across tagged paths these exclusions apply only to the selected route and preconditions, not every caller.

Final manifest admits many source catalogs, request histories and discarded archive payloads. Recover compatible Item/Done and raw/book code antecedents, retaining lossy normalization and merge fibers; no unique end-to-end inverse.
limitations: Seventeen exact tests run twice in debug and release; tests are bounded helpers and temp state/archive cases, not complete ingestion workflows.
GCS list and Duck process are compile/source evidence only. HTTP fetch/download and robots DNS/check routes are not executed.

state: Only explicitly selected routes execute; no automatic OAI-to-fetch pipeline exists. License labels preserve distinct raw/book domains until code transport. State files, raw pages and download manifests commit at different times; no composition-wide atomicity. Existing files precede STOP/cap checks in fetch. Catalog build can invoke DNS.
